reasoning: This is the OpenDataHub/RHOAI fork of MLflow. Upstream MLflow is also distributed as a Python SDK (with mlflow-skinny and mlflow-tracing under libs/), but in RHOAI it ships as a running service. Dockerfile.konflux, the Konflux build file, does three things: builds the React UI (mlflow/server/js, including a federated build served under /mlflow), builds the mlflow wheels, and packages them into a UBI9 runtime image. That image sets server-specific environment variables (MLFLOW_SERVER_ENABLE_JOB_EXECUTION, MLFLOW_ENABLE_AI_GATEWAY, MLFLOW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY) and installs postgresql-libs and sqlite for the backend store. It exposes port 5000 and starts with CMD `mlflow server --app-name kubernetes-auth --enable-workspaces --workspace-store-uri kubernetes:// --serve-artifacts`. The repo also has a Helm chart (charts/) with a Deployment, Service, Ingress, NetworkPolicy, ServiceMonitor, PVC and RBAC, which is how a long-running server gets deployed. The core of the project is a tracking server: Flask/FastAPI/gunicorn plus a database layer (alembic) and a web UI. FORK_HISTORY.md mentions operator version bumps, but those belong to a separate operator; this repo has no controllers or CRDs of its own. So the deployed RHOAI component is a service, even though the same code also works as a client library.
